sources: [S1] ISS (Institute for Standardization of Serbia) — ISO member since 1950, SRPS ISO 22400
[S3] Ciklopea localization blog — Latin script dominates digital/B2B in Serbia
[S3] The Translatery — Latin script dominance in Serbian tech/advertising
[S4] Serbian manufacturing case studies: Tetra Pak Serbia, confectionery OEE
[S5] terms.json — Serbian translations analyzed for consistency

falseFriends.fabric: Note: 'fabrika' correctly means 'factory' in Serbian (NOT a false friend)
falseFriends.performance: Use 'performanse' (accepted loanword) or 'učinak' for general performance
falseFriends.station: Use 'radna stanica' for workstation, not 'stanica' (bus/train station)
falseFriends.order: Use 'radni nalog' for production order, not 'red' (sequence)

grammarNotes.dualScript: Serbian uses both Cyrillic and Latin. Latin preferred for B2B software. NEVER mix scripts.
grammarNotes.compoundPluralModifiers: In compound noun phrases with genitive modifiers, prefer SINGULAR genitive for the modifier when it names a concept/category. PREFERRED: 'razlozi gubitka brzine' (reasons + loss [gen.sg] + speed [gen.sg]). CHECK: 'razlozi gubitaka brzine' — genitive plural 'gubitaka' may be governed by Serbian grammar. Flag for G3 native speaker review. Compare singular 'razlog gubitka brzine' — the modifier should ideally not change when only the head noun pluralizes.

industryContext.oeeTerminology: OEE (English acronym) is standard. No established Serbian equivalent.
industryContext.notEU: Serbia is NOT EU member — EN standards voluntary.

commonMistakes: Mixing Cyrillic and Latin scripts in same document
Script inconsistency — standardize to Latin for B2B

Compound plural modifier ambiguity: 'razlozi gubitaka brzine' vs 'razlozi gubitka brzine' — genitive plural 'gubitaka' vs singular 'gubitka'. Prefer singular modifier (names the concept); flag for G3 native speaker review
notes: OEE (English) standard. Latin script preferred for B2B (Cyrillic official but Latin dominates digital). Formal 'Vi'. Ekavian dialect. 7-case system.
